$comment: Single source of truth for which folders/files belong to which sellable edition.
4 buckets: shared (infra, always included, must never import UP into core/pro/premium),
core ⊂ pro ⊂ premium (each tier export includes shared + itself + everything below it).
Consumed by eslint.tier-boundaries.mjs (import-boundary lint) and scripts/export-tier.ts.
Known non-bugs (do not 'fix' by moving these): some folders intentionally hold Core-tier
capability today even though a sibling folder holds the Pro/Premium upgrade of the same
entity, because the underlying features are already split into separate folders:
- app/admin/warehouses (Core: single location) vs app/api/stock-transfers (Pro: transfers)
- app/admin/invoices (Core: manual PDF) vs lib/stripe + app/api/payments (Pro: online pay)
Where a folder can't be split cleanly yet (e.g. app/admin/user-management needs Core's
2-fixed-roles UI now and Pro's custom-role composer later in the SAME folder), that's a
signal for a future feature milestone to split the folder — not a manifest bug to fix now.
middleware/authMiddleware.ts is confirmed-dead legacy code (superseded by proxy.ts) —
bucketed as shared for now since it's harmless, flagged here as a deletion candidate.
KNOWN REAL GAP, unlike the two 'non-bugs' above — proven by `pnpm export:core` then, from
the output dir, `pnpm install && npx tsc --noEmit` (or symlink node_modules for a faster,
install-free check) — not theoretical. A first pass fixed the cleanly-mis-bucketed cases:
components/supplier moved core, lib/payments/order-payment-from-amounts.ts moved to
lib/invoices/order-payment-sync.ts (pure money-math, no Stripe import — was just mis-homed),
the 3 lib/server/support-ticket*-data.ts files moved into lib/support-tickets/,
types/catalog-insights.ts moved core (a core-shaped type with one optional Pro field —
lib/server/product-insights.ts had it computing that Pro field inline too; stopped doing
that and let the already-existing lib/insights/product-insights-enrich.ts wrapper own it,
same pattern lib/server/catalog-insights.ts already used), and
app/api/products/import/route.ts relocated to app/api/products-import/route.ts (out from
under core-bucketed app/api/products) with ProductImportDialog's fetch URL updated to match
— its hideImport gating prop already existed, no new UI pattern needed. Warehouse stock
summary (app/admin/warehouses/page.tsx) also fixed: dropped the blocking SSR
getWarehouseStockSummary call, left it to the existing client-side useWarehouseStockSummary
hook (already undefined-tolerant).

- app/api/products/route.ts PUT stock-reconcile mixes a core-relevant guard
(reservedCommitment vs new quantity, using core field Product.reservedQuantity) with
genuinely Pro warehouse-shrink planning (planCatalogQuantityReconcile /
applyCatalogQuantityReconcile against StockAllocation rows) in ONE request handler --
confirmed accurate, not stale (Phase 13, 2026-08-28): the two aren't separable call
sites, they're two fields of ONE input object to ONE pure function
(planCatalogQuantityReconcile), blended into a single reservedCommitment number. A
'Core is single-warehouse, simplify to single-row math' fix was considered and REJECTED
-- no hard single-warehouse constraint exists anywhere in code (verified by grep --
'Core: single location' above is a product-framing convention, not an enforced limit), so
a real Core customer with multiple StockAllocation rows could get silently misallocated
inventory from a naive simplification. A full 2-call split (modeled on the payments
precedent: useCreateCheckout() as a separate follow-up call against an already-created
id) was also considered -- architecturally correct, but changes the request/response
contract for EVERY tier, not just Core (hooks/queries/use-products.ts's
useUpdateProduct() would need to chain two requests) -- a live feature redesign, not
tier-export hygiene. DECISION: accept as documented debt, same class as the directly
comparable prisma/schema note below (lib/products/decrement-stock-allocations.ts) --
investigated and deliberately left alone, not silently skipped. Revisit only if Core's
warehouse feature set changes (e.g. a real single-warehouse constraint gets added).
Don't attempt a real Core sale without re-running the tsc check above and closing every item
it still lists — do not improvise fixes to any of the four above under time pressure.
prisma/schema/ (split multi-file schema, see prisma/schema/schema.prisma's own header) is
bucketed shared IN FULL, not tier-stripped model-by-model, even though each file's header
comment notes which tier's UI primarily owns it. Reason: octalve-ims runs one shared Postgres
database across every tier's codebase, and some Core-tier code has a real dependency on a
Pro-tier model today (lib/products/decrement-stock-allocations.ts reads/writes
StockAllocation for every order, Core included). Stripping prisma/schema/pro-only files out
of a Core export would break that code's `prisma generate` output. Don't split this bucket
without first removing that coupling.
